en: Although often credited with discovering the Philippines, Ferdinand Magellan actually died in the Battle of Mactan in 1521.
Emilio Aguinaldo did not write the Philippine Declaration of Independence; Ambrosio Rianzares Bautista actually authored and read the document.
Contrary to popular belief, the sampaguita, our national flower, is not native to the Philippines but was introduced from Asia.
Many mistakenly call the Senate the lower house, but the House of Representatives is actually the lower chamber of Congress.
While often called the last mambabatok, Whang-od is actually the oldest, actively training younger apprentices to continue the tradition.
Filipino and Tagalog are not exactly the same; Filipino is the national language that evolves by incorporating words from other languages.
Dr. Fe del Mundo did not invent the standard incubator, but she designed a makeshift bamboo incubator for rural areas without electricity.
Many believe Ati-Atihan is purely Christian, but it actually originated as a pre-colonial pagan tribute before adopting Santo Niño elements.
Freedom of speech in the Philippines is not absolute; it does not protect libelous, obscene, or dangerous false statements.
Jose Rizal did not write Noli Me Tangere in the Philippines; he actually finished the novel while living in Berlin.
Despite its common name, the Philippine monkey-eating eagle actually prefers to hunt flying lemurs and other animals, not just monkeys.
While famously depicted as moving a nipa hut, the Filipino value of bayanihan actually means any communal unity and cooperative work.
